subject.title: fix(infra): release exec-approvals locks across VirtioFS identity drift

question: Should this PR become the canonical exec-approvals VirtioFS repair, or should the overlapping implementation at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 remain canonical after a current-head comparison?
rationale: Both branches repair the same security-sensitive async sidecar-lock failure, but they differ in hardening history and proof; this is an ownership and merge-selection decision rather than a safe mechanical repair.

options.title: Compare and select one canonical PR
options.body: Compare the two current heads, require current-head VirtioFS evidence for the selected branch, then close or supersede the other implementation.

options.title: Prefer the live-proven branch
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 as the canonical repair if its reported live environment proof remains reproducible and this branch has no necessary hardening absent there.

options.title: Extract a maintainer-owned replacement
options.body: Create one maintainer-owned focused repair only if neither external branch can be adopted without duplicated protocol or insufficient authorization-boundary proof.

recommendation.title: Compare and select one canonical PR
recommendation.body: Compare the two current heads, require current-head VirtioFS evidence for the selected branch, then close or supersede the other implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the root-cause investigation and authored the overlapping async repair with reported real-environment validation.
